documents: Yang, Gomez, Schmid, Baringer 2022, Limnology and Oceanography Letters 7: 427-434, published paper (PDF)

entry.evidence: Net primary production (NPP) measurements in the open-ocean Gulf of Mexico are scarce and mostly limited to satellite-derived surface estimates.

steps.action: The authors name the gap: depth-resolved, year-round NPP in the open-ocean Gulf of Mexico is unknown, because existing estimates are satellite surface values or single-season field campaigns.
steps.quote: Field measurements of depth-resolved NPP in the open-ocean GoM are scarce and limited to a certain season

steps.action: They take from Pasqueron de Fommervault et al. (2017) the approach of adjusting uncalibrated float bio-optical data against satellite products to obtain a consistent dataset.
steps.quote: it is feasible to adjust the float measurements with satellite products

steps.action: They assemble archival Chl and bbp profiles from four BOEM floats (2012-2015, 237 profiles), compute mixed layer depth from float density, and match MODIS surface Chl, bbp and PAR to each profile.
steps.quote: A total of 237 profiles were used for this study

steps.action: Because the floats lacked nutrient sensors, they take monthly DIN climatologies from the co-author's GoMBio biogeochemical model and interpolate them to the float times and positions.
steps.quote: we used the model outputs (monthly climatology from 2012 to 2014) from GoMBio (Gomez et al. 2018)

steps.action: They check float surface (~8 m) Chl and bbp against satellite surface values. bbp matches in magnitude but shows no significant linear relation; Chl shows good linear relations (R 0.65-0.76) for all four floats.
steps.quote: no significant linear relationship was found between them

steps.action: They adjust the float Chl profiles with float-specific type II regressions against satellite Chl (Table 1) and leave bbp unadjusted to avoid artifacts.
steps.quote: the linear regression results shown in Table 1 were used to adjust the float Chl profiles

steps.action: They compute depth-resolved NPP with the carbon-based productivity model (Cphyto from bbp, growth rate from Chl:C and depth-attenuated satellite PAR), then average the estimates into monthly climatologies of 17-22 profiles each.
steps.quote: The carbon-based productivity model (CbPM; Behrenfeld et al. 2005, Westberry et al. 2008) was used to calculate the depth-resolved NPP

steps.action: They justify CbPM by the first author's earlier finding that float-based CbPM NPP in the western North Atlantic agreed with 14C incubation NPP.
steps.quote: float-based NPP estimates with CbPM had a good agreement with the NPP estimated

steps.action: They compare float-derived surface NPP with satellite CbPM NPP for 237 individual estimates (R = 0.71) and for monthly climatologies (R = 0.94), and judge the float NPP suitable for seasonal analysis.
steps.quote: The adjusted float data yielded surface NPP values close to the satellite estimates

steps.action: They compare the float surface NPP seasonal cycle (winter high, summer low) with earlier satellite and model studies and find it consistent.
steps.quote: with the seasonal pattern reported by former studies using satellite-based observations (Muller-Karger et al. 2015) and numerical models

steps.action: From the covariation with mixed layer depth and modeled nitrate, they attribute high winter surface NPP to nitrate from deep mixing, and name photoacclimation as a second factor in low summer surface NPP.
steps.quote: the winter high surface NPP was most likely due to the increased surface nitrate concentration from deep mixing

steps.action: They derive the 0-100 m integrated NPP climatology, which peaks in May (>500 mg m-2 d-1) and is lowest in December, a cycle different from the surface cycle.
steps.quote: Such seasonal variation is entirely different from the seasonal pattern of surface NPP

steps.action: They compare the May integrated NPP and profile shape with the 2017/2018 in situ experiments of Stukel et al. and Yingling et al. The profile shape is similar, but the float value is higher (~42 vs 24-29 mmol m-2 d-1).
steps.quote: the shapes of depth profile were similar

steps.action: They attribute the mismatch in absolute NPP to auxiliaries (spatial and temporal mismatch of the studies, lack of shipboard calibration), not to the estimate itself.
steps.quote: Possible explanations for the difference in the absolute NPP value includes the spatial/temporal mismatch of these two studies

steps.action: They set monthly NPP profiles and 0-20 m versus 20-100 m integrals against modeled DIN and PAR profiles to trace which factor tracks each layer's seasonal change.
steps.quote: Because the decrease of deeper layer (20–100 m) NPP was more significant than the increase of 0–20 m NPP

steps.action: They keep the interpretation that nutrient supply controls surface-layer NPP and light controls the 20-100 m layer, which contributes more to total NPP for most of the year.
steps.quote: there is no nutrient limitation in the deeper layer

steps.action: For a July mid-depth (~50 m) NPP peak, they propose lateral nutrient transport (river plume or Loop Current eddies) over vertical mixing, and as an alternative, lateral transport of organic matter. Neither is tested.
steps.quote: Alternatively, such high NPP signal at mid-depth could also be a result of the lateral transport of organic matter

steps.action: They conclude with the first year-round depth-resolved float NPP dataset for the open-ocean GoM, noting uncertainty in absolute values from the missing calibration and the model parameterization.
steps.quote: this year-round depth-resolved NPP dataset provided us a useful tool to study the seasonal and vertical distributions of NPP

end.claim: Adjusted float data give the first year-round depth-resolved NPP for the open-ocean GoM: surface NPP peaks in winter and 0-100 m NPP in May, with the 20-100 m layer contributing most of the year.

decisive_move.sentence: Applying CbPM to the satellite-adjusted float Chl and unadjusted bbp profiles produced the depth-resolved NPP; every claim rests on this estimate.

gates.evidence: Action: the floats were deployed by BOEM for a Lagrangian study of deep circulation (p. 428), not to test an NPP hypothesis. Claim: the float NPP was tested against satellite NPP (p. 430), but float Chl had already been regressed onto satellite Chl, so the test is partly circular. The in situ comparison showed a mismatch that was absorbed by auxiliaries (p. 431). The layer-control claims were read from covariation and not tested. Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: photoacclimation (reduced light-harvesting pigment under high light)
type II linear regression for float-satellite adjustment

novelty_claims.quote: used to obtain the first year-round depth-resolved NPP estimates in this area
With the adjusted Chl and unadjusted bbp, for the first time we obtained

limits: Composition is none_fits. The walk is an estimation from archival data: observe, calibrate, infer, compare, then interpret. The monthly cycle is repeated by nature, but no regularity is fitted, so natures_repetition does not fit. No rival is excluded, and no new capability is built (the adjustment approach is cited). Sub-claims: the layer controls (nutrient at the surface, light at depth) and the winter mixing explanation are best_explanation, inferred from covariation with modeled DIN (a co-author's model climatology, not measured) and PAR. The July mid-depth peak is left with two untested rivals (no_conclusion on that sub-question). Absolute NPP values are acknowledged as uncertain. The 50% quantile bars describe spread, not a full uncertainty budget. The paper reports no sensitivity tests of CbPM parameters, the bbp conversion exponent, or the MLD criterion. Inference: because float Chl was regressed on satellite Chl, the float-satellite NPP agreement is not independent. The paper does not say how the 237 profiles were chosen from eight deployed floats, nor why only four floats were used. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded.

disagreements.target: [...] et al. 2021; Yingling et al. 2021 (April-May 2017/2018 in situ NPP experiments)
disagreements.support: Float-based May integrated NPP (~42 mmol m-2 d-1) exceeds the in situ 24-29 mmol m-2 d-1, but the profile shapes agree; the difference is attributed to spatial and temporal mismatch and missing calibration.
disagreements.quote: Possible explanations for the difference in the absolute NPP value includes the spatial/temporal mismatch of these two studies

disagreements.target: Satellite-based surface NPP studies of the open-ocean GoM (e.g., Muller-Karger et al. 2015)
disagreements.support: The depth-integrated NPP cycle peaks in May, unlike the winter-peaking surface cycle, so surface-only estimates misrepresent water-column production.
disagreements.quote: Such seasonal variation is entirely different from the seasonal pattern of surface NPP, which indicates the importance of obtaining depth-resolved NPP data

disagreements.target: GoMBio model DIN climatology (Gomez et al. 2018)
disagreements.support: The climatological model DIN does not show the mid-depth nutrient supply implied by the July mid-depth NPP peak.

alternatives_considered.chosen: Carbon-based productivity model (CbPM, updated Westberry et al. 2008)
alternatives_considered.reason: CbPM satellite global product is widely used and available for comparison; float CbPM NPP agreed with 14C incubations in Yang et al. 2021

alternatives_considered.chosen: Adjust float Chl by regression on satellite Chl; leave bbp unadjusted
alternatives_considered.alternatives: adjusting float bbp against satellite bbp
alternatives_considered.reason: no significant linear relationship for bbp; to avoid any potential artifacts

alternatives_considered.chosen: Low summer surface NPP mainly from low surface nitrate in a shallow stratified mixed layer
alternatives_considered.reason: surface NPP follows MLD and modeled nitrate seasonality

alternatives_considered.chosen: July mid-depth NPP peak most likely from lateral nutrient transport (Mississippi plume, Loop Current eddies)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: vertical mixing; lateral transport of organic matter
alternatives_considered.reason: MLD was still shallow, so vertical mixing is less likely; organic matter transport offered as an untested alternative
